ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Compulsory identification and verification of all directors, officers and individuals with significant control under CBCA and FINTRAC guidance. Mandatory screening against the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list, Global Affairs Canada lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the Criminal Code Part II.1 terrorist entity list, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list, and, as cross-border best practice, the US OFAC SDN list and UK/EU consolidated lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, with source-of-wealth verification; the screening result must be documented in the Stage 1 formation file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada – Online Filing Centre (ISED) / NUANS Name Search and Reservation service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the CBCA and the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, a corporate name must be distinctive and not confusing, followed by a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., Limitée, or a prescribed abbreviation. The name may be in English, French, or both official languages; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters for the NUANS search. The use of numerals and initials is permitted, but the resulting name must contain a clearly distinctive element.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Insurance, Loan, Finance, Broker, and other financial-services terms requiring approval from OSFI or the relevant financial institution regulator
Canada, Canadian, Federal, Government, Crown, Royal, Parliament, Senate, and any term implying official government sponsorship or authority
University, College, Institute, Hospital, Medical, Pharmacy, and other regulated professional/health terms requiring provincial or professional regulatory consent
Law, Legal, Engineer, Engineering, Accountancy, or other reserved professional designations
Obscene, scandalous, or contemptuous expressions, and names that are otherwise contrary to public policy
Any name that is identical or confusingly similar to a prior NUANS record, permissible registered name, trademark, or official mark
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS report and any name reservation are valid for 90 days. A reservation may be renewed for a further 90-day period by filing a new/amended reservation before expiry. If the Director refuses a proposed name, the applicant may (i) submit a revised distinctive element and a new NUANS report without loss of priority; (ii) within 30 days of refusal, request reconsideration in writing from the Director of Corporations Canada with supporting trademark and rationale; and (iii) if reconsideration is unsuccessful, apply to the Federal Court for judicial review within 30 days of the final refusal. Alternatively, the incorporator may file articles under a designated-number name to preserve incorporation timing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A commercial registered-office or virtual-office arrangement is permissible only if the service provider maintains a physical street address in Canada at the registered office province, accepts service of process and mail during business hours, and can make corporate records available as required under CBCA section 20. A post-office box or a pure virtual mailbox without a Canadian physical address is not acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% or less annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a no-licence digital-health-app corporation with no AML red flags. The probability rises to roughly 25% if the company later handles personal health information that triggers a PIPEDA complaint, receives a FINTRAC reporting/record-keeping query, or is selected for a Corporations Canada compliance examination.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 3, 6, 8, 9 and 19
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 3 under the Canada Business Corporations Regulations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA; consideration for shares may be money, property or past services; no escrow requirement for this digital health software issuer.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscription of 100 common shares by the sole incorporator at CAD 0.01 per share is accepted, and share certificates are issued accordingly. 2. The registered office is established at [full address], Province of [Province], and the registered representative is retained. 3. The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until removed by the Board. 4. A corporate seal and banking resolutions are adopted, and management is authorized to complete ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search or Numbered Company Election
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre / Licensed NUANS search house
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search for 'health fitness app' distinctive name, or elect a numbered corporation name 'Corporation No. 1234567 Canada'; submit the name request within the incorporation filing if a distinctive name is desired.
required_dossiers: NUANS preliminary name search report (if distinctive name is used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged, submit a new name request with alternate marks or proceed with the assigned numbered name; no additional incorporation fee re-application beyond the original if refiled promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles and Statutory Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel or licensed filing agent acting under Corporations Canada rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 3 Articles of Incorporation specifying franchise, business purpose, share structure, maximum number of directors, and any restrictions on share transfers; prepare Form 4 Notice of Registered Office and Form 5 Notice of Directors; obtain director consents on Form 6.
required_dossiers: Form 6 – Consent to Act as Director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If articles are deficient, Corporations Canada issues a deficiency notice; correct and resubmit within the stated deadline; the filing date is preserved where corrections are made before rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application through Corporations Canada's secured portal; upload the articles and notices, declare the initial registered office and directors, and pay the CAD 200 filing fee by credit card or online payment; receive an electronic acknowledgment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the Registrar's requisition through the same portal within 30 days; if the query is not resolved, file corrective articles or amendments before restarting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada registry / in-house corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance, retain the online Certificate of Incorporation, convene an organizational meeting of the sole director/incorporator, adopt the first board resolution, adopt by-laws, issue shares, approve banking resolution, and complete minute book entries.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate cannot be obtained due to discrepancies, submit a formal correction request to Corporations Canada with supporting affidavit and applicable fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with CRA for a federal Business Number, corporation income tax account, GST/HST account (if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000), and payroll deductions account if hiring staff; provide corporation registration details and certify director information.
required_dossiers: Estimated annual revenue and GST/HST registration threshold assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA account registration encounters profile mismatch, call CRA business enquiries with the corporation's legal name and registration number to reconcile the account within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Extra-Provincial Registration and Office Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial corporate registry in operating province (e.g., Ontario ServiceOntario, BC Corporate Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File extra-provincial registration in each province where the corporation carries on business; in Ontario, file upon establishing a business presence or leasing office; in Quebec, complete the Registraire des entreprises declaration; ensure workplace safety board registration (e.g., WSIB/WorkSafeBC) if employing workers.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address in operating province
Employer payroll and workers' compensation registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If provincial registration is delayed or rejected, file remedial declarations and pay late fees; request a waiver for deviation only if administrative error is proven.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – pure digital health app; no physical industrial or manufacturing plant.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operating or manufacturing permit required under federal or provincial law for software-as-a-service fitness tracking.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); principal digital channel is the CRA My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html); GST/HST registration executed via 'Register with CRA' using Form RC1 or through accredited tax software; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers customs export reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A federal or provincial Business Corporation receives a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with program accounts upon incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act; the CRA issues the initial BN package automatically. A foreign entity registering from abroad must complete Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) and file it by mail to the Sudbury Tax Centre, or use the online non-resident GST/HST registration service, attaching constitutional documents, board authorization, and identity verification material; a GST/HST program account (RT prefix) is then opened. Non-resident digital vendors may register under the simplified GST/HST vendor registration regime without a permanent establishment in Canada by using the CRA's 'GST/HST registration for non-residents' web application and designating an authorized representative. Processing ranges from immediate electronic notification for eligible online filings to 5–15 business days for paper submissions; the BN serves as the single statutory identifier for corporate income tax (RC account), GST/HST (RT account), payroll (RP account), and customs transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Business Corporation is a per-se taxpayer resident in Canada, taxed on worldwide income under Income Tax Act (ITA) s. 2(1) and s. 250; no U.S.-style pass-through or check-the-box classification is available. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) is eligible for the small business deduction under ITA s. 125, but the entity itself remains the taxable person. Non-resident-owned Canadian corporations file T2 returns and are subject to Part I tax plus Part XIII withholding on outbound payments where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada; classification follows statutory corporate status. Relevant elections include: (i) alternate currency/reasonable allocation election under ITA s. 261 (Form T657); (ii) associated-CCPC allocation election under ITA s. 136; (iii) ITA s. 216 election for non-residents to report Canadian rental income on a net basis; (iv) ITA s. 115(1) election for non-residents disposing of taxable Canadian property; (v) hybrid mismatch rules codified at ITA ss. 18.4–18.6 denying deductions in structured cross-border hybrid arrangements per BEPS Action 2; (vi) GST/HST s. 273 election for closely related registrants treating intercompany taxable supplies as made for nil consideration; and (vii) voluntary GST/HST registration election for suppliers below the small-supplier threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax at 5% federal; Harmonized Sales Tax in participating provinces: Ontario 13%, Nova Scotia 15%, New Brunswick 15%, Newfoundland and Labrador 15%, Prince Edward Island 15%; British Columbia and other non-participating provinces apply 5% federal GST only; Quebec applies QST at 9.975% on a GST-inclusive base). Digital health and fitness app subscriptions, in-app purchases, and telemetry data services are taxable digital supplies subject to place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — mandatory GST/HST registration is triggered when taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) made in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. For non-resident digital suppliers under the simplified vendor registration regime, the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies to 'specified supplies' (digital products, services, and goods delivered in Canada via mail or courier) calculated on worldwide revenue attributable to Canadian-resident recipients. Suppliers below the threshold may register voluntarily to recover input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate exists in Canada; the CRA does not operate an API-based invoice stamping or continuous transaction control (CTC) system. Mandatory e-invoicing is not imposed at the federal level. Taxpayers must retain complete electronic records and invoices in legible, machine-readable format under ETA s. 286 and ITA s. 230; CRA accepts EDI and PEPPOL BIS 3.0 documents, particularly for voluntary B2G transactions. For digital app transactions, the supplier must preserve at least two elements of place-of-supply evidence: IP address of the acquiring device, SIM card country code, billing address on file, home address of the customer, or transaction metadata from the payment processor. When distribution is made through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, the platform may be deemed the GST/HST supplier for Canadian transactions under ETA ss. 211.19 et seq.; the Canadian corporation must retain the platform agreement, settlement reports, and underlying supply-chain data to demonstrate compliance and correct ITC entitlement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Digital health/fitness app services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI Part V when the recipient is a non-resident at the time of supply and the supply is not in respect of tangible personal property in Canada, real property in Canada, or a service to be performed in Canada (intangible personal property rule in Sch. VI Part V s. 10; software downloads delivered electronically follow the place-of-supply rules in s. 5.1 of Sch. IX or the special digital-supply rules). Physical branded hardware exported from Canada is zero-rated under Sch. VI Part V s. 1 provided the supplier holds evidence satisfactory to the Minister that the goods were exported within 60 days of the supply (or the extended period allowed by the Minister). Zero-rated exports preserve full input tax credits and typically generate refunds when ITCs exceed output tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A / CAED or CBSA EDI manifest) for any exported physical goods valued over CAD 2,000; goods valued at or below CAD 2,000 generally do not require a B13A filing
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or courier shipment record evidencing delivery to a foreign destination and third-party signature/clearance
Sales agreement, end-user license agreement, or subscription contract identifying the non-resident recipient and confirming the supply is not for use in Canada

Inward remittance certificate, bank settlement record, or payment processor financial report (e.g., Apple IAP or Google Play settlement statements) tracing the export consideration to the non-resident customer
Two-element digital evidence under CRA place-of-supply guidelines: customer billing address plus IP address, SIM card country code, device location, or payment processor country code
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory 180-day export-proceeds repatriation law; the 180-day measure is applied here as an internal audit benchmark for documentary completeness and transfer-pricing commercial substance, as income is recognized on the accrual basis in Canadian dollars under ITA s. 261. For incorrect zero-rating: CRA may reassess within 4 years for GST/HST (ETA s. 298) and 3 years for income tax (ITA s. 152(3)); the period is extended to 6 years for negligence and is unlimited where misrepresentation is attributable to fraud or wilful default. Applicable penalties include: (i) ETA s. 280 failure-to-collect/remit penalties up to the tax collectible plus daily interest; (ii) false-claim penalty of 50% of the overstated refund or input tax credit under ETA s. 285.1; (iii) ITA s. 163(2) gross negligence penalty of 50% of the understated income tax; (iv) director personal liability for unremitted amounts under ITA s. 227.1 and ETA s. 323; and (v) criminal prosecution for evasion with fines up to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment under ITA s. 239 and ETA s. 327. Clawbacks are retroactive, with statutory daily-compounded interest at prescribed CRA rates and no ministerial discretion to waive where documentation is fabricated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free floating exchange rate regime with unrestricted convertibility for current account transactions. Capital account transactions are permitted subject to Bank of Canada notification or approval thresholds for certain foreign direct investments. Profit remittances to shareholders are unrestricted for resident Canadian corporations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender obligation applies to digital service exports or app-related revenue as these constitute current account transactions. For goods exports only, foreign exchange proceeds must be surrendered to an authorized foreign exchange dealer within 90 days of receipt under the Export and Import Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability. Electronic money institutions are regulated by OSFI under the Payment Services Act. Cross-border issuance of e-money for a health app faces licensing, capital, and consumer protection constraints.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is permitted for standard operational accounts using digital ID verification. In-person appearance or video KYC interview is required for directors or authorized signers in higher-risk cases or when transaction volumes exceed thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership or control structure opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry search, articles of incorporation, shareholder agreements, and beneficial ownership declarations

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction connections or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of funds and source of wealth documentation, transaction history, and independent legal opinions

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 191 (Capital Contribution) or 210 (Equity Injection). Verification requires board resolutions, incorporation documents, and shareholder approvals. All transactions must satisfy FINTRAC AML/KYC obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit for documentary trade. Digital service disbursements to vendors or affiliates are processed via bank channels with proper invoicing and purpose codes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director General, Corporations Canada - Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late fee for single omission; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers a Notice of Intent to Dissolve, and the corporation may be administratively strike-off after a resolution process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 6th month after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month deferred, up to 12 months; further prosecutable penalties for non-filing under Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue/asset threshold under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA). An independent auditor is mandatory for distributing (reporting) corporations. A non-distributing corporation may waive audited statements only if all shareholders consent at each annual meeting; otherwise an auditor must be appointed and audited financial statements presented.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises (distributing corporations); private non-distributing corporations may apply Canadian ASPE (Part II of CPA Canada Handbook) or optionally adopt IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under s.21.1 CBCA, the corporation must maintain an accurate Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC). At least annually, before the fiscal year-end anniversary, the corporation must review and update share transfers to confirm each ISC's identity, shareholding percentage, ownership date, and any cease-to-control events. The register must be retained at the registered office, but no separate government filing is required unless the corporation is a prescribed entity or a distributing corporation under securities rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Register of Members (Shareholders) and Share Transfers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 185 - 550 per year (C$250 - C$750) for a Canadian corporate agent and registered office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 12,000 for a private digital health app (if audit cannot be waived)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal corporate income tax general rate after federal abatement and General Rate Reduction; 9% federal small-business rate for Canadian-controlled private corporations on qualifying active business income up to the Small Business Deduction limit. Provincial and territorial corporate income tax rates apply separately.
